items.title: Obama's first inauguration
items.line: 20 January 2009. Obama and Chief Justice Roberts fumbled the oath, so they redid it in the White House Map Room the next day. Aretha Franklin sang in a Swarovski-bowed hat.

items.title: Chillwave gets a name
items.line: In July 2009 the satirical blog Hipster Runoff coined "chillwave" to poke fun at hazy, reverb-soaked bedroom acts. Washed Out, Neon Indian and Toro y Moi got the label anyway.

items.title: Death of Michael Jackson
items.line: He died on 25 June 2009, aged 50. TMZ broke it, Google blocked searches for 30 minutes, and Twitter and Wikipedia both reported crashes.

items.title: Susan Boyle
items.line: Her Britain's Got Talent audition aired 11 April 2009. She sang I Dreamed a Dream, and within nine days the clip had 103 million views across 20 sites.

items.title: Glee
items.line: The pilot aired on Fox on 19 May 2009. Ryan Murphy, Brad Falchuk and Ian Brennan's show-choir series went on to win six Primetime Emmys.

items.title: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 2
items.line: Out 10 November 2009. Activision reported US$310 million in the US and UK on day one, the biggest entertainment launch in history at that point.

items.title: Avatar
items.line: Released 18 December 2009 in the US, with 2,032 of 3,457 theaters showing it in 3D. It passed Titanic on 25 January 2010 and finished near $2.9 billion.
